market: Friday was a rout led by AI and chip stocks: SPY fell 3.64% to 689.81, QQQ 5.67%, and IWM (the small-cap ETF) 2.88% to 256.61, its worst week since April 2025 at about -7.5%. The VIX closed at 35.89, up 26%, the 10-year yield eased to 4.91% as money moved to safety, and crude rose 1.2% to $83.41. The S&P 500 and Dow are now in correction, and reports tie the selling to AI valuations and spending, with small caps hit as part of a broad cut in risk after a week of rate worries. Most small-cap decliners on tonight's list fell with no news of their own. Next week is short (closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, half day Friday), so volume will be thin. In this tape I favour names with their own reason to rise and no funding need: a cluster of insiders buying after a reset, and a cash-rich stock sold hard on no news.

verdicts.name: OFRM
verdicts.thesis: Five insiders including the CEO bought about $816k of stock near $12 this week, after the toddler-bar recall and a guidance cut took it 53% off its high. The bad news is out and quantified (Q4 is a known loss quarter, 2027 guided to at least $330M sales and break-even), the rest of the range is selling steadily, and the company has $106M of cash and no debt. It fell less than IWM on Friday, and more Form 4s may land next week.
verdicts.dilution: Cash $106.4M at Sept 30, no debt; the credit line and convertible notes were repaid or converted at the February IPO. No ATM, follow-on, open warrants or convertibles found. The 180-day lock-up expired in August, so early holders are free to sell. The recall may cost up to $30M, not yet in results; insurance recovery unconfirmed.
verdicts.wrong_if: The recall widens (more products, a new FDA action or a retailer pulling the brand), or a securities class action or share sale is filed, or the stock closes below the insiders' buying range near $11.50.
